summary: Static Kubernetes NetworkPolicy templates and rendered snapshots for messenger, mail, social, and community FD-001 dogfood tenant workload charts, defaulting app Pod ingress to the Oyatie gateway namespace and egress to DNS plus OTLP namespace seams only.
claim_boundary: This slice adds source-controlled Kubernetes NetworkPolicy templates/snapshots and values defaults for FD-001 backbone dogfood workload charts. It proves static chart/snapshot network-boundary intent and CI-smoke regression coverage only; it does not claim Kubernetes API admission, live CNI installation/enforcement, namespace-label admission, actual traffic isolation, service mesh authorization, Gateway reachability, DNS/OTLP availability, ArgoCD sync/health, branch-protection state, remote CI green, or production tenant workload deployment. FD-001 product delivery remains the master-plan product goal; Oyatie Cloud is the future dogfood substrate/proof point.

best_practice_research.used_for: Grounds additive NetworkPolicy behavior, pod/namespace selectors, ingress/egress policy types, and the need for a CNI plugin to enforce policies.
Grounds network isolation as one component of Kubernetes tenant isolation alongside RBAC, quotas, and admission controls without claiming a live cluster.
Confirms this slice composes with existing restricted-style Pod posture while staying focused on L3/L4 policy intent.

repo_local_context.use: Current FD-001 dogfood charts had Deployments, Services, disabled-by-default HTTPRoutes, ServiceAccounts, labels, resources, probes, runtimeClassName, topology spread, and token automount hardening, but no NetworkPolicy template/snapshot in this chart surface.
Older/non-dogfood chart surfaces already model default-deny/allowlist network policy patterns, supporting network policy as an expected microservice hardening artifact.
Backbone CI smoke parses FD-001 dogfood chart seams and now blocks missing NetworkPolicy templates/snapshots and missing tenant/cost labels/non-claim posture.

findings: Small chart/snapshot hardening with no new controller, runtime dependency, service code path, API schema, or data migration.
Uses values-controlled namespace names for gateway, DNS, and OTLP seams rather than embedding a live-cluster claim.
Static app NetworkPolicies make future FD-001 tenant workload boundaries explicit for ingress/egress review.
The claim remains static/source-controlled; no live CNI enforcement, namespace-label admission, or traffic isolation proof is asserted.
A RED static check failed before implementation for every service: missing networkPolicy values, missing NetworkPolicy templates, and missing rendered NetworkPolicy snapshots.
Governance smoke now semantically parses rendered NetworkPolicies and fails if policy types, app selectors, gateway ingress, DNS/OTLP egress, labels, or non-claim annotations are missing.
Operators can find the static network-boundary knobs under networkPolicy values with safe default-enabled posture for the dogfood chart surface.
Source templates and rendered snapshots remain parseable YAML/Helm text and preserve tenant/cost labels plus explicit static-only non-claim annotations.
CI smoke parses 60 files after adding NetworkPolicy templates and rendered snapshots.
Rejected claiming namespace-wide default deny because this chart does not prove release namespace ownership or live namespace admission; app-Pod selector is safer for static dogfood charts.
Rejected broad 0.0.0.0/0 egress defaults; future DB, broker, object-store, or vendor egress must be explicitly added with live evidence.
Rejected service-mesh authorization changes here because L7 identity/policy enforcement is a separate live substrate slice.
No secrets, credentials, cloud identities, or tenant data are added.
Rendered policy defaults ingress to the oya-gateway namespace and egress to kube-system DNS plus observability OTLP namespace seams only.
NetworkPolicy labels and non-claim annotations reduce the chance static manifests are misread as live CNI enforcement evidence.
No Rust runtime, SQL, broker, gRPC, REST, or hot-path code changes. Kubernetes metadata only.
NetworkPolicy templates and snapshots carry existing tenant, cost-center, workload-class, regulatory-pack, dogfood-substrate, and product-goal labels for future audit/cost/policy correlation.
Rollback removes the NetworkPolicy templates/snapshots, values block, and CI smoke checks without data migration or public API impact.
Default egress keeps an OTLP namespace seam visible, but no live telemetry is emitted by this static slice.
No Deployment selectors, Service selectors, image references, or runtime ports change.
Live rollout that requires DB, broker, object storage, SMTP, or vendor egress must add explicit allow rules and evidence rather than relying on ambient egress.
Uses existing CS-BACKBONE slice naming and <service>-network-boundary resource names.
Updates task plan/todo and multispectrum evidence only; no new root Markdown or retired external coordination surface.
Network boundary posture lives in per-service Kubernetes Helm chart directories and static rendered dogfood snapshots.
Infrastructure chart contract only; no domain/usecase/adapter boundary drift.
No Cargo, npm, Helm dependency, container, or provider dependency changes.
No data schema or algorithm changes. New values are under networkPolicy.
Backbone governance smoke now blocks missing NetworkPolicy templates/snapshots and rendered policy regressions for all four FD-001 dogfood workloads.
